name: Autoimmune Autonomic Ganglionopathy

criteria.description: Subacute or acute onset of widespread autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, gastrointestinal dysmotility, anhidrosis, urinary retention)
No alternative explanation for autonomic failure
Response to immunotherapy (IVIG, plasma exchange, or immunosuppression)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Subacute/acute onset pandysautonomia with positive gAChR antibodies; seronegative forms exist and are diagnosed by clinical criteria and exclusion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: gAChR antibodies are found in ~50% of cases. Seronegative AAG can still respond to immunotherapy. Antibody levels correlate with disease severity.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subacute onset pandysautonomia (combined orthostatic hypotension, GI dysmotility, sicca, and pupillary dysfunction)
pathognomonic.notes: The combination and subacute onset are distinctive; gAChR antibodies confirm when present

laboratory: Ganglionic acetylcholine receptor (gAChR) antibodies positive (~50% of cases)
Antibody titers correlate with severity (>0.20 nmol/L suggestive, >1.0 nmol/L highly specific)
May have other autoimmune markers (ANA, thyroid antibodies)
imaging: CT abdomen may show dilated bowel loops in severe GI dysmotility
other: Autonomic reflex testing: severe combined sympathetic, parasympathetic, and sudomotor failure
QSART: absent or markedly reduced sweat output

distinguishingFeatures: PAF has gradual onset over years, not subacute
PAF is a synucleinopathy, not autoimmune
PAF does not respond to immunotherapy
MSA has prominent motor features (parkinsonism or cerebellar ataxia)
Diabetic neuropathy develops gradually with longstanding diabetes
AAG has subacute onset regardless of diabetes status

redFlags: Subacute onset of severe pandysautonomia (consider paraneoplastic cause)
Associated malignancy (especially small cell lung cancer) should be excluded
Concurrent sensory neuropathy or encephalopathy (expand antibody testing)
Failure to respond to immunotherapy (reconsider diagnosis)
references: Vernino S, et al. Autoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy. Handb Clin Neurol. 2022;186:205-218.
Golden EP, et al. Autoimmune autonomic neuropathies and ganglionopathies: epidemiology, pathophysiology, and therapeutic advances. Clin Auton Res. 2019;29(3):277-288.
Nakane S, et al. Autoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy: an update on diagnosis and treatment. Expert Rev Neurother. 2019;19(10):953-965.
